title: vellum.ai: What the Personal AI Assistant Does
summary: Vellum.ai launched a personal AI assistant for its agent platform. Understand what new capabilities it adds and how it integrates with your workflows.
body_markdown:
## What workflow connections vellum.AI enables today


Today you can connect vellum.ai only through general parts, such as an HTTP request step, an AI step pointed at a custom provider, or an MCP server, none of them confirmed as native. We checked the platform's repository and catalog on 2026-11-04 and found nothing specific to vellum.ai, so there's no native connector.


We haven't run vellum.ai ourselves, so everything below is a design to test, not a verified recipe.


Each step up adds a part that can break, and the three options run from least setup to most. Decide first who owns the connection, because every option needs a credential held by a named person or service account.


### Connect vellum.ai with an HTTP request step


You need an endpoint vellum.ai documents for starting work, plus a token scoped to that action only. Store it as a secret in the workflow, owned by a service account rather than an individual.


What could fail: the token belongs to someone who leaves, the endpoint changes without notice, or the call returns before the work finishes and the workflow carries on with an empty result.


### Connect vellum.ai with a custom provider AI step


If vellum.ai doesn't expose an OpenAI-compatible interface, a base URL and a key, this option is closed. When it does, compatibility is often partial, so tool calls or streaming may behave differently from what the step expects.


The step also sends your workflow data to a third party, so check what the key permits before pointing it at records.


### Connect vellum.ai assistant through an MCP server


An MCP server that exposes vellum.ai's assistant or tools needs a host to run it and a credential for each tool it exposes.


What could fail: the server's an extra service someone must patch and monitor, and its permissions can be broader than the task needs. Review the tool list before you connect it.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) covers the workflow side of this, where the assistant needs something to call.


Once a integration is connected in a project, an agent can use it: the same integration action that runs as a step in a flow is also exposed as a tool on that project's MCP server, which any MCP-capable client can use, whether that is Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent of your own.


Nothing is exported or registered a second time for any of the 747 integrations, which matters here because a catalog you must re-integrate for your agents is a second migration.


The mechanism sits in packages/integrations in the open source repo, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it.


Only the first option is worth trying before you have answers on vellum.ai's interface; the other two depend on it.
